posts.title: New project: vibe-coded multiplication game, and a lot of thoughts about this whole LLM fad!
posts.description: I “wrote” a game to practice multiplication – check it out , and stick around afterwards to watch me get surprisingly angsty about it! ( a reminder that I don’t use LLMs to help me write , this post included!) My kids are learning multiplication at school, and need more practice. We’ve made flash cards in the past, but thought it would be fun to have a little game they could play to track their progress. This is the kind of thing that I would normally write a little web app for, but I wanted it to be pretty (not my forte!) and the kids had a deadline coming up soon. So I bit the bullet, signed up for a home Claude Code subscription, and had it write it. Unsurprisingly it was very quick and did a good job! You can see the chat transcript : it wasn’t quite a one-shot, but it was pretty close. I have a lot of feelings about this! I cannot overemphasize how easy this was: I went from an idea to a working app in 20 minutes. It has cute SVG animals that move around, confetti effects, and lit

posts.title: Station Eleven review – good, creepy
posts.description: Station Eleven by Emily St. John Mandel My rating: 4 of 5 stars After enjoying The Last Murder at the End of the World , I thought I might be sufficiently removed from the (real) pandemic to enjoy reading about a (fictional) pandemic! And it was fine at first, but I eventually did get kinda creeped out. I’ve been feeling a bit more upbeat about the world in general after the midterms, so the fact that this was a bit much for me is some combination of my being forever scarred by the pandemic (possible!) or Mandel’s excellent work in painting a terrifying picture. Anyway, it was good! Might try some of her other books next. View all my reviews

posts.title: Remaking movies versus remaking video games
posts.description: Whenever Disney announces they’re doing a live-action remake of a beloved animated movie, I roll my eyes and wonder why they felt the need to do that (obviously, the money). But I realized I don’t feel the same way about remakes of video games, and tried to figure out why. One reason is that I can pull out my copy of The Lion King (1994) and it’s still a great movie! I suppose for some movies better CGI and whatnot can make it look better, but most movies didn’t use a lot of CGI back then…because it looked bad! But a 20-year old video game looks much less pretty than a remake that came out today. Another thing is that newer video games have a lot more modern conveniences than in the old days; better map systems, inventory management, saving, etc. This does depend a bit on the quality of the remake, but in general it’s so much easier to add this stuff these days.
